name: CA-31
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 8-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Cisneros's large fundraising edge over Eric Ching

model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Cisneros: an incumbent in a district that leaned Democratic by 8 points, running in a favorable environment, with a roughly seven-to-one fundraising advantage and no outside spending against him. Markets price his win odds near 95%, so the forecast stays in Safe D territory with only a modest trim for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing Ching within single digits would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gil Cisneros, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election against Republican Eric Ching in a Southern California district that voted Democratic by about 8 points at the presidential level. Cisneros has raised roughly $705,000 and holds a large cash advantage, while Ching has raised under $100,000, and no significant outside spending has entered the race on either side.

With no public general-election polls and no expert ratings, the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which favor Cisneros heavily. Prediction markets put his win chances around 95%, consistent with a comfortable double-digit expected margin in a favorable Democratic environment.
